## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

1	# ngrrram
2	
3	`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
4	particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
5	layouts effectively.
6	
7	![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)
8	
9	Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
10	these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
11	example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
12	Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
13	making strong use of ngrams.
14	
15	There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
16	[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
17	inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.
18	
19	However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
20	which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
21	layout I was still learning.
22	
23	Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
24	ones.
25	
26	## Installation
27	
28	### Releases
29	
30	Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
31	linux, windows and macos are available.
32	
33	### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))
34	
35	Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:
36	
37	```bash
38	yay -S ngrrram-git
39	or
40	yay -S ngrrram-bin
41	```
42	
43	### From Source
44	
45	Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:
46	
47	```bash
48	cargo build --release
49	```
50	
51	The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`
52	
53	### Looking for help packaging!
54	
55	If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!
56	
57	## Usage
58	
59	`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
60	flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.
61	
62	Options:
63	```
64	Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]
65	
66	Options:
67	  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
68	  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
69	  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
70	  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
71	  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
72	  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
73	      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
74	      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
75	      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
76	      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
77	      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
78	  -h, --help              Print help
79	```
80	
81	If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
82	```bash
83	ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
84	```
85	
86	## Layout Emulation
87	
88	To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
89	`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
90	the second one being the one you want to emulate.
91	
92	Available layouts are:
93	
94	- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
95	- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
96	- `azerty`    (Azerty)
97	- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
98	- `colemak`   (Colemak)
99	- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)
100	
101	> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
102	> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
103	> If you know a solution, please tell me.
104	
105	## Random Notes
106	- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
107	  that lesson; no need to stress.
108	- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
109	  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PTY harness to run ./executable and interact with it."""
import os, pty, sys, time, select, argparse, fcntl, termios, struct, signal

def run(args, keys=None, wait=0.5, rows=24, cols=80, outfile=None, final_wait=1.0):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execv("./executable", ["./executable"] + args)
    # set window size
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))
    out = b""
    def drain(duration):
        nonlocal out
        end = time.time() + duration
        while time.time() < end:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
            if r:
                try:
                    chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not chunk:
                    break
                out += chunk
    drain(wait)
    if keys:
        for k in keys:
            os.write(fd, k if isinstance(k, bytes) else k.encode())
            drain(0.15)
    drain(final_wait)
    # capture final state
    if outfile:
        with open(outfile, "wb") as f:
            f.write(out)
    os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    try:
        os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    except OSError:
        pass
    return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--args", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--keys", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--wait", type=float, default=0.5)
    ap.add_argument("--final-wait", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=80)
    ap.add_argument("--outfile", default=None)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    keys = a.keys.split(",") if a.keys else None
    out = run(a.args.split() if a.args else [], keys, a.wait, a.rows, a.cols, a.outfile, a.final_wait)
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(out)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render snapshots of a raw PTY capture at N evenly spaced points."""
import sys
from vt import Term

data = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
rows = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 24
cols = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 80
n = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 5
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    cut = len(data) * i // n
    t = Term(rows, cols)
    t.feed(data[:cut])
    print(f"===== snapshot {i} (byte {cut}/{len(data)}) =====")
    print(t.render())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the ordered ngram list by sweeping -t (top) from 1 upward.
At each top=k, sample lessons until an item appears that was not in the
top-(k-1) set; that item is rank k. Stops when the list is exhausted."""
import sys, time, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace")
from driver import Session

def sample(nval, top, combi):
    s = Session(["--nokb", "-n", str(nval), "-t", str(top), "-c", str(combi), "-r", "1"])
    s.pump(0.22)
    items = s.lesson_text().split()
    s.close()
    return items

def extract(nval, combi, maxrank=200, max_retries=300, log=sys.stderr):
    ordered = []
    known = set()
    k = 1
    while k <= maxrank:
        found = None
        retries = 0
        while found is None and retries < max_retries:
            items = sample(nval, k, combi)
            retries += 1
            new = [x for x in items if x not in known]
            if len(new) > 1:
                # multiple unknowns: we missed ranks; take first, log warning
                print(f"WARN k={k}: multiple new {new}", file=log)
            if new:
                found = new[0]
        if found is None:
            print(f"EXHAUSTED at k={k} after {retries} tries; list size {len(ordered)}", file=log)
            break
        ordered.append(found)
        known.add(found)
        if k % 20 == 0:
            print(f"k={k} found={found!r} retries={retries}", file=log)
        k += 1
    return ordered

if __name__ == "__main__":
    nval = sys.argv[1]
    combi = int(sys.argv[2])
    start = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 1
    end = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 200
    # prefix mode: if start>1, we assume earlier ranks unknown; instead we
    # just collect the SET for top=start-1 first, then do ordered discovery.
    known = set()
    ordered = []
    if start > 1:
        # collect set for top=start-1 with many samples
        stale = 0
        while stale < 40:
            before = len(known)
            known.update(sample(nval, start - 1, combi))
            stale = 0 if len(known) > before else stale + 1
        print(f"prefix set size for top={start-1}: {len(known)}", file=sys.stderr)
    k = start
    while k <= end:
        found = None
        retries = 0
        while found is None and retries < 400:
            items = sample(nval, k, combi)
            retries += 1
            new = [x for x in items if x not in known]
            if len(new) > 1:
                print(f"WARN k={k}: multiple new {new}", file=sys.stderr)
            if new:
                found = new[0]
        if found is None:
            print(f"EXHAUSTED at k={k}; size {len(ordered)}", file=sys.stderr)
            break
        ordered.append(found)
        known.add(found)
        if k % 10 == 0:
            print(f"k={k} found={found!r} retries={retries}", file=sys.stderr)
        k += 1
    print(json.dumps(ordered))
